steps.title: Coat dishes with poly‑L‑lysine
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1 mg/mL poly‑L‑lysine solution from a 10 mg/mL stock, add enough to cover each well (≈1 mL per well), wrap dishes in foil and incubate overnight at room temperature, keeping the solution from drying (turn blower off).

steps.title: Wash coated dishes
steps.instruction: Aspirate the poly‑L‑lysine, add 1 mL sterile water, aspirate; repeat this wash three times, then aspirate the final water and let the dishes dry completely under the hood.

steps.title: Prepare dissection materials and media
steps.instruction: Autoclave or ethanol‑sterilize instruments, set up 60‑mm dishes with HBSS dissection medium, and label 15 mL tubes with 1 mL (individual) or 5 mL (pooled) dissection medium.

steps.title: Dissect embryos and isolate brain
steps.instruction: Euthanize E16.5 embryos by decapitation, place heads in dissection medium, remove skin, open the skull at the base, lift off the skull halves, extract the brain, and peel off all meninges completely.

steps.title: Isolate cortical tissue
steps.instruction: Make a sagittal cut to split the brain, remove the hippocampus and striatum (identified by C‑shape and opacity), and retain only the cortex.

steps.title: Transfer cortices to tubes
steps.instruction: Place each cortex in a 15 mL tube containing 1 mL dissection medium (individual) or combine two cortices in 5 mL dissection medium (pooled), keeping tissue submerged and working quickly.

steps.title: Collect tail for genotyping
steps.instruction: For individual cultures, excise a small piece of tail from each embryo and store for later genotyping.

steps.title: Prepare digestion medium
steps.instruction: Mix 125 µL DNase I (10 mg/mL stock) with 10 mL 0.025% Trypsin‑EDTA (or 0.05% Trypsin as noted) to obtain the digestion solution.

steps.title: Digest cortices with trypsin/DNase
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of digestion medium to the dissection medium (1 mL for individual, 5 mL for pooled), then incubate at 37 °C for exactly 30 min.

steps.title: Inactivate trypsin and triturate cells
steps.instruction: Add dissociation medium (2 mL individual, 5 mL pooled) to inactivate trypsin, centrifuge at 1200 rpm for 5 min, resuspend in 2 mL (individual) or 4 mL (pooled) dissociation medium, and triturate gently 20 times with a P1000 pipette avoiding bubbles.

steps.title: Filter, centrifuge and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Pass the suspension through a cell strainer, centrifuge at 700 rpm for 7 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 2 mL (individual) or 4 mL (pooled) culturing medium.

steps.title: Count cells and plate neurons
steps.instruction: Take 15 µL of the suspension, mix 1:1 with Trypan Blue, count cells (typical yield ~2 × 10⁶ cells/mL, viability > 80 %), then plate 5.0 × 10⁵ cells per well of a 6‑well plate in 2 mL pre‑warmed culturing medium.

steps.title: Maintain neuronal cultures
steps.instruction: Every 5 days, aspirate one‑third of the medium from each well and replace with fresh, pre‑warmed (37 °C) culturing medium; do not replace the entire volume.

steps.title: Induce mitochondrial depolarization
steps.instruction: Treat cultures with 10 µM Antimycin A and 1 µM Oligomycin (dissolved in DMSO) for 3–9 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Lyse neurons for protein extraction
steps.instruction: Aspirate medium, wash twice with 1 mL warmed DPBS containing protease inhibitors, phosphatase inhibitors, and 200 mM chloroacetamide, place plates on ice, add 50 µL lysis buffer per well, scrape cells, and collect lysate in a 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Sonicate and incubate lysates
steps.instruction: Sonicate lysate with a probe sonicator for 5 s at 20 % amplitude, then incubate on ice for 30 min.

steps.title: Clarify lysates and store
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 17000 g, 4 °C for 30 min, collect supernatant, determine protein concentration with a Coomassie assay, and store lysates at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare samples for SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Dilute 40 µg lysate 4‑fold in 4× LDS loading buffer supplemented with fresh 10 % 2‑mercaptoethanol, then boil for 3 min at 97 °C (or 20 min at 37 °C) without over‑boiling.

steps.title: Run NuPAGE gel
steps.instruction: Load samples onto a Nu‑PAGE Bis‑Tris 4‑12 % gel and run at 120 V for approximately 2 h.

steps.title: Transfer proteins to membranes
steps.instruction: Transfer to PVDF membrane for phospho‑ubiquitin/ubiquitin and to nitrocellulose for phospho‑Parkin/Parkin using Towbin buffer at 80 V for 1.5 h on ice or in a cold room; use only one membrane per transfer tank.

steps.title: Block membranes
steps.instruction: Incubate membranes in 5 % milk in 0.1 % TBS‑Tween for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibodies
steps.instruction: If antibodies are in 5 % BSA, rinse membranes twice with 0.1 % TBS‑Tween, then add primary antibodies diluted as follows in 0.1 % TBS‑Tween: phospho‑ubiquitin 1:2000, ubiquitin 1:1000, GAPDH 1:5000, Parkin 1:1000 (all in 5 % BSA); phospho‑Parkin 1:2000 in 5 % milk. Incubate overnight at 4 °C (pre‑incubate phospho‑Parkin antibody with a membrane for 2 days if desired).

steps.title: Wash membranes after primary
steps.instruction: Wash membranes three times with 0.1 % TBS‑Tween, 10 min each.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Incubate with HRP‑conjugated secondary antibody diluted 1:5000 in 1 % BSA (0.1 % TBS‑Tween) for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash membranes after secondary
steps.instruction: Wash membranes three times with 0.1 % TBS‑Tween, 10 min each.

steps.title: Develop and image blots
steps.instruction: Apply ECL western blotting reagents, develop the signal, and capture images with a Chemidoc (or use film for higher sensitivity if needed).
